title: 2022 building code energy and accessibility standards adopted (New South Wales)
summary: NSW applied the NCC 2022 commercial energy efficiency and condensation provisions from 1 October 2023, raised its own BASIX energy standards for homes to the NCC 2022 level instead of adopting the code's, and did not adopt the livable housing provisions.

instruments.title: National Construction Code 2022
instruments.provisions: energy efficiency, condensation management and livable housing design provisions (Volumes One and Two, the ABCB Housing Provisions and the Livable Housing Design Standard)

instruments.title: Environmental Planning and Assessment (Development Certification and Fire Safety) Regulation 2021 (NSW)
State Environmental Planning Policy (Sustainable Buildings) 2022 (NSW) (BASIX)
instruments.provisions: BASIX thermal and energy standards, used in place of the NCC 2022 housing and apartment energy efficiency provisions

commenced.what: NCC 2022 adopted as a whole; its energy efficiency, condensation management and livable housing provisions started later (the dates below)

Commercial energy efficiency and condensation management provisions applied; housing and apartment energy standards raised to the NCC 2022 level through an enhanced BASIX; livable housing design not adopted

direction_rationale: The 2022 code raised minimum energy performance for new homes to 7 stars and added livable housing design requirements. Design and compliance costs are partly fixed per dwelling and may fall hardest on small builders, lowering entry and raising exit.
comparison: Staggered and partial adoption, October 2023 to May 2025 (NSW and WA did not adopt livable housing; Tasmania did not adopt housing energy efficiency; the NT kept 5 stars)

Adopting laws are those the state's schedule in NCC 2025 names (data/processed/ncc/regulatory_map.json).

assessment.summary: Adopts the 2022 National Construction Code's higher energy efficiency (7-star) and livable housing standards for new homes. New South Wales raised energy standards through its own BASIX scheme and did not adopt livable housing. The standards cut running costs and improve access, which are not weighed here; they also add to the cost of building.

marks.reason: Adds design and compliance costs to every new home, which weigh most on small builders.
Adopting only part of the national code, or a local version, leaves builders working across states with different rules.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission estimates housing construction regulation costs about 1% of GDP a year.

responsible.note: Produces the National Construction Code that each jurisdiction adopts.

history.what: The Australian Government announced a pause on further residential changes to the NCC until mid-2029, after NCC 2025, except essential safety and quality changes, keeping the 2022 residential standards, including 7-star energy efficiency.
